about: Hand facts for tools/dungeon-run-catalog that the inputs do not hold. Every exclusion needs a reason; a theme list replaces the keyword tags of its labelKey (first tag primary).

adaptations.note: A dual-class (Tombs of Terror) run drafts from both classes, but the engine's Discover and random pools follow the primary class (Classes[0]) only. The exceptions are the explorer treasures' own class Discovers (ULDA_301 Map of Uldum, ULDA_303 Starseeker's Tools), which offer cards of both row classes (RunContext.PlayerClasses). Other Tombs secondary-class generation is not modelled.

ULDA_011 VIP Membership ('Taverns you visit are upgraded!', phase 6 F13): the client data does not say what an upgraded tavern is (the original was server-side). In SoloStone an upgraded tavern gives 1 more gold and offers 1 more option (DungeonRun.VipExtraGold, DungeonRun.VipExtraOffers); the treasure has no match effect.

Step 9 treasure audit (D6, one treasure economy): a generic adventure treasure, one scoped to every starter of its adventure whose text assumes no hero, deck or hero power, is "shared" (run-v1.json). Only a run of schedule stamp 4 (acts-v4h, acts-v4t; DungeonRun.Tuned) reads the flag: there the treasure is offered to every loadout (DungeonRun.TreasureInScope), weighted as affine only by its tags outside its own adventure; every released schedule keeps the scoped offers. A shared treasure's upgrade stages are shared too. Step 9 treasure audit (D6): the adventure treasures that stay scoped, with the reason. Hero-specific Monster Hunt treasures (scoped to one hunter's deck: GILA_501, GILA_503, GILA_506, GILA_507, GILA_508, GILA_509, GILA_510, GILA_513, GILA_511, GILA_602, GILA_603, GILA_604, GILA_605, GILA_607, GILA_608, GILA_610, GILA_611, GILA_612, GILA_401, GILA_403, GILA_410, GILA_411, GILA_412, GILA_413, GILA_414, GILA_415, GILA_901, GILA_903, GILA_904, GILA_906, GILA_907, GILA_910, GILA_911, GILA_913) name or need their hunter's mechanic (Tess's weapons and Scavenge, Darius's Cannons, Shaw's Bloodhounds and Beasts, Toki's spells). Signature treasures (Tombs of Terror) are a row's loadout, never drafted. Two generic texts replace the run's hero power and so assume a power that can be replaced: DALA_738 A Prince's Ring (a random Death Knight power at match start) and ULDA_306 Stolen Titan Secrets (the boss's power for the rest of the run); on a Monster Hunt hunter or a Tombs explorer that power is the row's identity and its own treasures read it, so both stay with their adventure. The SoloStone and Dungeon Run treasures were never scoped by adventure and are unchanged.

Step 9 (D9): GILA_BOSS_43t Grave Mistake, the spell The Witchwood's Monster Hunt dropped for beating Gravekeeper Damph, is Damph's own reward: run-v1.json row with reward true (offered false, runs v4: never drafted) and encounters-v1.json gila_43_damph v4 reward. On a run of schedule stamp 4 a won fight against Damph (not on the last node or in a finale) adds it to the run deck as a treasure card (origin treasure, never a tavern target) before the floor's treasure draft, once per run (DungeonRun.GrantEncounterReward). The card is the boss card itself (scripted in DungeonRunEncounters.F11.cs and admitted for the run player and the boss by DungeonRunAdmission.F11.cs), not a run content shell. With no room in the deck (deckMax) it becomes 1 banked gold, spent at the next tavern. Released schedules never grant it.

Step 9 (D5): on a run of schedule stamp 4 a bundle draft skipped because the deck has no room (deckMax), and a boss reward with no room, each become 1 banked gold (DungeonRunState.BankedGold), added to the next tavern's gold and then cleared (DungeonRunTavernNode.Open). Acts II and III of acts-v4h and acts-v4t open no bundle draft after a treasure-draft floor or the major (bundleAfterTreasure false, D5 variant (b)): a skip by design, which banks nothing. The original adventures had no such conversion; it is a SoloStone choice so that a full deck still gains something from a won fight.

Step 9 (D4, D5): on a run of schedule stamp 4 every tavern option is offered at one weight per act (tavern-v1.json weightByAct 3), so the 14 Dalaran Heist and 8 Tombs of Terror options split the offers about 64 : 36 (the released weights gave about 75 : 25); DALA_902 Remove a Card is weighted 5 in act III, where the deck is largest; DALA_904 Good Food is bought at most twice a run (maxPerRun 2, counted from DungeonRunState.HealthBonus, and the knobs cap HealthBonus at 10 the same way). The original weights and caps are unknown (server-side); these are SoloStone numbers.

customBucketsAbout: Phase 6 (F16): themed SoloStone-curated pool entries for the classes no original adventure offered (Death Knight, Demon Hunter), so an act run's fourteen drafts never run dry under any pick order (seven entries each; the phase 6 review walked always-pick-last runs that fell to 2 offers on floors 13-14 with four. The Death Knight entries share cards, as the rune-free Death Knight cards admitted are few). Members are admitted, scripted, rune-free collectible cards of the class (the catalog tool fails the build on any other); each entry is taken at most draft.bucketMaxTakes times.
